around.headline: Bengaluru pothole leaves a woman needing plastic surgery, as city rolls out 'jet patcher' machines
around.summary: A woman needed plastic surgery after a fall caused by a Bengaluru pothole, per The News Minute, even as the state government begins deploying 'jet patcher' machines that spray hot asphalt into small potholes without closing the road, per India Today, The Hindu and TOI. If you ride a two-wheeler, treat every unlit or rain-hidden stretch as a potential hazard until repairs actually reach your route.
around.source: The News Minute, India Today, The Hindu

around.headline: Bengaluru holiday firm and four people booked for cheating a government official of Rs 1.7 lakh
around.summary: Police have booked a travel/holiday firm and four individuals for allegedly cheating a government official of Rs 1.7 lakh, per Deccan Herald. A reminder to verify any travel agency's registration and pay only to its official account before handing over a full package price.

around.headline: Private bus operators hike fares ahead of the festival rush
around.summary: Private bus operators are raising ticket prices ahead of the festival season, per Public TV English — book intercity travel early or compare against railway/KSRTC options if the private fare jump stings.

around.headline: Faulty timing displays on the metro's Yellow Line are frustrating commuters
around.summary: Commuters on Bengaluru Metro's newly launched Yellow Line are facing hassles due to malfunctioning arrival-time displays at stations, per Deccan Herald. Worth building in extra buffer time until the displays are fixed rather than trusting the platform countdown.

around.headline: Nine held, including three Central Jail staff, for smuggling mobile phones into a Bengaluru prison
around.summary: Police busted three separate cases of mobile phones being smuggled into Bengaluru's Central Jail, arresting nine people including three jail staff, per Deccan Herald and The New Indian Express. A reminder that jail-security lapses like this are what let phone-based scams and extortion rackets keep running from behind bars.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Aadhaar OTP helps trace a Bengaluru student missing for seven months
around.summary: A Bengaluru teenager who vanished after leaving for college was traced seven months later after an Aadhaar-linked OTP flagged her location, per The New Indian Express and The Indian Express. If a family member goes missing, flag it to police early so Aadhaar and phone-linked trails can still be pulled.
around.source: The New Indian Express, The Indian Express

street_smart.title: You're booking a family holiday package — flights, hotel and a car — through a travel agency you found via a WhatsApp group, echoing today's news of a Bengaluru holiday firm booked for allegedly cheating a government official of Rs 1.7 lakh. The agent asks you to transfer the full ₹1.5 lakh package cost right now to their personal UPI ID, promising the official booking confirmation and GST invoice will follow 'within a day' — and that the festival-season discount only holds if you pay today. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru story: police booked a holiday/travel firm and four people for allegedly cheating a government official of Rs 1.7 lakh, per Deccan Herald. This scenario widens that into the common mechanism behind travel-booking fraud: full advance payment to a personal account before any verifiable confirmation exists. Travel/holiday-package scams haven't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The agent is friendly, has a well-reviewed Instagram page, and is pushing you to pay immediately before the 'discounted' price expires tonight.

choices.text: Pay only a small token booking amount now, and send the balance to the travel company's registered business account (not a personal UPI ID) only after you receive PNRs, a hotel confirmation number, and a GST invoice carrying the firm's registration details.
choices.feedback: Correct. This is exactly what breaks the mechanism in today's case: money sent to a personal account with no verifiable booking has no paper trail to chase if the firm disappears. A GST invoice and confirmed PNRs before full payment give you a legal and financial trail if something goes wrong.

choices.text: Transfer the full ₹1.5 lakh right away to the agent's personal UPI ID to lock in the festival discount, since the page has good reviews.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Personal-account transfers and a 'pay now or lose the discount' deadline are the two classic pressure points scammers use — good reviews can be bought or built up for months before an agency vanishes with advance payments, which is the pattern behind cases like today's.

choices.text: Ask a couple of friends who've used the same agency before, and go ahead if they vouch for it.
choices.feedback: Risky. Word of mouth lowers the odds of a scam but isn't proof — a firm can deliver fine for months and still cheat a customer later, or a friend's 'good experience' might just mean they haven't been let down yet. Verify registration and get written confirmation regardless.

choices.text: Pay half the amount upfront and the rest after the trip, assuming that limits how much you could lose.
choices.feedback: Risky. Paying less upfront reduces the damage but doesn't fix the real problem — if the firm was never verified and there's no written confirmation, you still can't force a refund. Document first, then decide how much to pay, not the other way around.

takeaways: Verify a travel agency's registration (GSTIN, and for larger tour operators, Ministry of Tourism or IATA recognition) before paying anything.
Pay only to a firm's registered business account or official payment gateway — never to an individual's personal UPI ID, however trustworthy they seem.
Treat 'pay right now or lose the discount' as a red flag in itself; a legitimate agency can hold a quote for at least a few hours while you verify PNRs and a GST invoice.

quiz.question: What technology is Bengaluru now deploying to fix small potholes without shutting down the road?
options: Jet patchers that spray hot asphalt into the pothole
quiz.why: Jet patchers heat and blast bitumen and aggregate directly into the pothole from a moving vehicle, so crews can patch small potholes in minutes without closing a lane to traffic.

quiz.question: China has confirmed Xi Jinping will visit India for the first time in how many years, as BRICS talks get underway in Delhi?
quiz.why: Xi's last visit to India was the 2019 informal summit with PM Modi in Mamallapuram, near Chennai.

quiz.question: What kind of digital trail helped police trace a Bengaluru student who had been missing for seven months?
quiz.why: Aadhaar-linked OTP verification — typically triggered when the person uses their Aadhaar for a SIM, bank, or government service — can flag a fresh location even months after someone goes missing.

quiz.question: Karnataka's Vidhana Soudha, home to the state legislature, is built primarily from which locally quarried stone?
quiz.why: Completed in 1956 in the Neo-Dravidian style, Vidhana Soudha remains one of the largest state legislative buildings in India.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Oxygen makes up about 21%, with argon, carbon dioxide and trace gases accounting for the small remainder.
